headline: SHORT ORDER SHOUT gets walkie-talkie voice and a host who can bench a seat
lede: The online kitchen's last rough edges are gone: the host can demote a lagging friend to CPU (and promote them back) mid-shift without breaking the hash law, mic arm + phone push-to-talk shipped, and — a salvage story — the engine half arrived from a dead lane's unpushed worktree.

notes.text: #1416 final stage merged: tick-anchored DEMOTE/PROMOTE seat chips (every box flips at the same sim tick) + voice production (M arms the mic, phone MIC/VOX chips, echo etiquette refuses double-talk). soslinkcheck grew 86 -> 133 assertions; the arrival-anchored mutant goes red exactly where determinism lives.

Cross-lane salvage: slot b died mid-edit without pushing; its worktree held a near-complete draft of the design it posted on #1416. Slot a rebuilt it as its own commits, credited b, and the new proof tier caught an off-by-one the draft would have shipped (promote deadlocked at the flip tick — resume boundary fixed one pump ahead).

Also fixed: the online keyboard was DEAF — the net key branch returned every key, so arrows/Space/V were unreachable mid-shift online (and so were VirtualControls events on phones). Play keys now fall through.

Environment note for the next lane: this Mac's DNS is poisoned and headless Chrome SIGABRTs (session services dead). The session ran on a DoH proxy + curl-based gh shim — source /tmp/forge/netenv before any network command; browser tiers only run on CI.
